extracted.intended_audience: adult aspiring fiction writers and creative writers seeking workshops or coaching
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and expectations for multi-week fiction and journaling classes and workshops (novel, short story, generative writing, and journaling), including what will be taught, what participants will produce, and how feedback will be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel elements: point of view, character, conflict, setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the text to discuss elements of fiction such as point of view, character, conflict, and setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course will work together to understand 'what makes a novel work—and how you might translate that knowledge to your own pages.' Focus is on translating analysis of a model novel into students' own writing; generative exercises produce new material based on prompts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular generative practice and time commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you’ve never written creatively before or you’re a more experienced writer looking for a recharge, your mission in this course is simple: devote three hours a week to your writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Through engaging exercises you'll 'mine memory and imagination' to build characters, settings, dialogue, select point of view, and explore voice across genres. Expected outcomes include fresh drafts, new ideas, and a stronger sense of voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story precision and economy
rubrics_metrics.description: The short story is a precise and powerful form, where every detail matters and each moment shapes the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction focuses on using each detail to shape the whole story and on the particular demands and possibilities of the short story form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short story craft elements: theme, character, motif, structure, point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ll explore how we can give stories deeper resonance using key elements of fiction writing—theme, character, motif, structure, and point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes combine close readings with focused craft discussions and workshopping to apply these elements to student stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop feedback criteria: content questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Content questions: 'How does this character challenge or reflect expectations?' 'What themes emerge from the story’s events?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback will probe thematic and character-related choices to clarify stakes, character function, and emergent themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop feedback criteria: craft questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft questions: 'Is this the best point of view for this story?' 'Is this the best length for this amount of story?' 'Are the events being revealed in the best order?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feedback attends to structural and craft decisions (POV, length, order of revelation) to help develop revision strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active participation in workshop
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers will actively participate in shaping the workshop, not just listen passively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants are expected to engage in discussion, offer feedback to peers, and help shape workshop priorities rather than remaining passive listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission length and revision expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: You will have the opportunity to write or revise at least two complete stories (up to 25 pages each) and receive detailed written feedback from the instructor and your peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete production goal (two complete stories up to 25 pages) plus written feedback supports substantive revision work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of published work as models
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ll study work from The Best American Short Stories 2025 ... and read and discuss short pieces of published writing by authors including Margaret Atwood, Gwendolyn Brooks, and Mary Oliver to spark ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Close readings of published work are used to generate craft insights and inspiration that students can apply to their own writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral sharing and on-the-spot feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Each session includes time to discuss the writing process and share work aloud for supportive, on-the-spot feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sessions emphasize immediate, spoken responses alongside written feedback to foster generative momentum and peer support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative focus over critique (novel class)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our focus will be on generative writing and mutual support rather than critique or workshopping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel class prioritizes producing new scenes and building momentum rather than detailed line-by-line critique; intended outcome is collection of new material and craft insight to continue independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability, motivation, and peer support
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ll check in about struggles and victories, share strategies for staying motivated, and build momentum together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructor-led accountability and peer encouragement are treated as part of craft development and sustaining a writing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journaling habit support and community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Journaling with Kayleigh community, we tackle the two biggest stumbling blocks of journaling – loneliness and boredom. With our mix of chat, live events, monthly themes, and downloadable resources, you’ll find inspiration and community every day to grow a consistent, fulfilling habit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community features (chat, live events, monthly themes, downloadable resources) are presented as supports for developing a consistent journaling practice across formats (diary, commonplace book, morning pages, scrapbook).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-session prompt sprints (Free Draft Generator)
rubrics_metrics.description: In this one hour session, you’ll have the opportunity to respond to engaging writing prompts, share your work with others, and receive information about upcoming workshops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, prompt-driven sessions are positioned as entry points for generating seeds of projects, connecting with community, and discovering longer workshops; registration required though session is free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coaching availability and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: I am available for individual and small group coaching online and in person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coaching is offered for writers who do not find a suitable class; rates and suggested topics available elsewhere, implying tailored, goal-oriented instruction beyond structured classes.
